title: National Parks Deal with Damage After Government Shutdown
titleZh: 政府停摆后国家公园处理受损情况
credits: The Associated Press reported this story. Ashley Thompson adapted it for VOA Learning English, with additional materials from Smithsonian.com. Caty Weaver was the editor.

sentences.en: Many of America’s national parks remained open during the country’s longest-ever government shutdown.
sentences.zh: 在美国史上历时最长的政府停摆期间，许多国家公园仍然开放。

sentences.en: But few had enough National Park Service employees working to protect the areas and keep watch of visitors.
sentences.zh: 但很少有公园有足够多的国家公园局员工来保护这些区域并照看游客。

sentences.en: Those visitors did a lot of damage in 35 days.
sentences.zh: 这些游客在35天内造成了大量破坏。

sentences.en: They walked over sensitive lands.
sentences.zh: 他们踩踏了敏感的土地。

sentences.en: They opened gates while no one was watching.
sentences.zh: 他们在无人注意时打开大门。

sentences.en: One person even struck one of California’s famous Joshua Trees with a vehicle.
sentences.zh: 有人甚至用车撞击了加州著名的约书亚树之一。

sentences.en: When park service employees returned to work last week, they began cleaning up and repairing what they could.
sentences.zh: 上周国家公园局员工返回工作岗位后，他们开始清理并尽可能修复受损设施。

sentences.en: But environmental experts warn that the damage in some places could take years to recover.
sentences.zh: 但环境专家警告说，某些地方的破坏可能需要数年才能恢复。

sentences.en: Even before the shutdown, national parks faced $12 billion in much-needed repair work.
sentences.zh: 即使在停摆之前，国家公园就面临着急需的120亿美元修复工作。

sentences.en: That number has only grown.
sentences.zh: 这一数字还在不断增长。

sentences.en: Many parks had no employees working during the shutdown.
sentences.zh: 许多公园在停摆期间没有员工在岗。

sentences.en: Others had skeleton crews..
sentences.zh: 其他公园只有少量精简人员。

sentences.en: Local governments and nonprofit organizations offered money and volunteers during the shutdown, which began on December 21 and ended on January 25.
sentences.zh: 在始于12月21日、终于1月25日的停摆期间，当地政府和慈善组织提供了资金和志愿者。

sentences.en: National Park Service spokesman Mike Litterst told reporters that the damage was not widespread.
sentences.zh: 国家公园局发言人迈克·利特斯特告诉记者，破坏并不普遍。

sentences.en: He said most visitors took good care of the land.
sentences.zh: 他说大多数游客都很好地保护了土地。

sentences.en: But interviews with park officials and nonprofit groups that help keep parks running tell a different story.
sentences.zh: 但对公园官员和协助维持公园运转的慈善组织的采访却讲述了不同的故事。

sentences.en: Angie Richman is a spokeswoman at Arches National Park in Utah.
sentences.zh: 安吉·里奇曼是犹他州拱门国家公园的一位女发言人。

sentences.en: She said visitors left human waste outside a bathroom, walked on trails within an area that was off-limits to visitors and damaged an entrance gate.
sentences.zh: 她说，游客把人类排泄物丢在卫生间外，在禁止游客进入的区域内的小径上行走，并损坏了一个入口大门。

sentences.en: At Joshua Tree National Park, an off-road vehicle ran over one of the park’s special trees.
sentences.zh: 在约书亚树国家公园，一辆越野车碾压了公园的一棵特殊树木。

sentences.en: Several other Joshua trees were damaged, including one that was spray-painted.
sentences.zh: 其他几棵约书亚树也遭到了破坏，其中一棵被喷了漆。

sentences.en: A former Joshua Tree National Park ranger told Smithsonian.com that it could take 200 to 300 years for the park to fully recover from the shutdown damage.
sentences.zh: 前约书亚树国家公园护林员告诉史密森尼网站，该公园完全恢复.shutdown造成的破坏可能需要200到300年。

sentences.en: At Great Smoky Mountains National Park, visitors cut locks on some gates to closed roads and stole about $5,000 in repair tools, spokeswoman Dana Soehn said.
sentences.zh: 大烟山国家公园发言人达娜·索恩表示，游客剪断了部分封闭道路的锁，并偷走了约5000美元的维修工具。

sentences.en: Employees at Death Valley National Park in California found human waste and toilet paper all across the desert.
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚州死亡谷国家公园的工作人员在沙漠各处发现了人类排泄物和卫生纸。

sentences.en: Park officials also found evidence of people kicking in locked bathroom doors.
sentences.zh: 公园官员还发现了有人踢开锁着的卫生间门的证据。

sentences.en: And a high-speed video on Death Valley’s Facebook page showed how it took staffers two hours to clean a bathroom overflowing with trash and covered with waste.
sentences.zh: 死亡谷的Facebook页面上的一段高速视频显示，工作人员花了两个小时才清理完一个堆满垃圾、被排泄物覆盖的卫生间。

sentences.en: Workers at Death Valley National Park must replant in areas damaged by off-road vehicles.
sentences.zh: 死亡谷国家公园的工作人员必须在被越野车辆损坏的区域重新植树。

sentences.en: All of this delays much-needed repairs in other areas of the 1.3 million-hectare park.
sentences.zh: 这一切都推迟了这座占地130万公顷的公园其他急需的修复工作。

sentences.en: David Blacker is chief of the Death Valley Natural History Association.
sentences.zh: 大卫·布莱克是死亡谷自然历史协会的主管。

sentences.en: He told the Associated Press, “It became pretty depressing the kinds of things people will do when they are unsupervised.”
sentences.zh: 他告诉美联社：“当人们无人看管时，他们会做出各种各样的事情，这变得相当令人沮丧。”

sentences.en: At some parks, the lack of people meant animals moved in.
sentences.zh: 在一些公园，缺乏游客意味着动物们搬了进来。

sentences.en: A colony of elephant seals took over a Northern California beach in Point Reyes National Seashore.
sentences.zh: 一大群象海豹占据了加利福尼亚北部金门国家休闲区的一处海滩。

sentences.en: There were no workers there to prevent the animals from gathering in the popular tourist area.
sentences.zh: 那里没有工作人员阻止动物们在热门旅游区域聚集。

sentences.en: Park rangers and volunteers are now leading small groups of visitors to safely see the seals and their young.
sentences.zh: 公园护林员和志愿者现在正带领小批游客安全地观赏这些海豹及其幼崽。

sentences.en: The possibility of another shutdown remains.
sentences.zh: 再次关闭的可能性依然存在。

sentences.en: President Donald Trump and Congressional leaders agreed to a temporary spending bill that re-opened the government for three weeks.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统与国会领导人达成了一项临时拨款法案，使政府重新开放三周。

sentences.en: Trump has said another shutdown could start February 15 if he and Democratic leaders cannot agree on money for a U.S.-Mexico border wall.
sentences.zh: 特朗普表示，如果他和民主党领导人无法就美墨边境墙的资金达成一致，另一次关闭可能在2月15日开始。

sentences.en: I’m Ashley Thompson.
sentences.zh: 我是阿什利·汤普森。
